core.title: Delegate user/system flow execution from the FlowRouterRunner to the FlowRunner; never execute product capabilities in flow router code
core.given: An application module defines a FlowRouterRunner (route control)
core.when: you add or change anything in that module (imports, action handling, user/system flow execution)
core.then: Resolve one admissible user/system flow and delegate its execution to the FlowRunner's execute entry point (roles.runtime_components#user_system_flow_runner_execute); the FlowRouterRunner must never execute product capabilities itself.
prefer: Delegate instead of executing: resolve the admissible user/system flow for the action, then hand that user/system flow to the FlowRunner and return the result of its execution — do not loop over the steps yourself
avoid: Importing a product capability entry module anywhere in the FlowRouterRunner module
Invoking a direct user/system-flow-execution entry point from flow router code

Iterating a user/system flow's step sequence — its ordered steps — as an executor loop; the sequence containment field and the executor-loop idiom are per-stack profile data (roles.plan_hierarchy#user_system_flow_step_sequence, idiom.source_syntax#step_executor_loop)
Otherwise invoking product capability steps, choosing the next step inside a user/system flow, or bypassing the FlowRunner
unless: The production FlowRunner itself is the legitimate wagon-step executor; its own step loop is exempt
core.why: Flow router is route control, not execution: the FlowRunner is the single component that runs product capabilities and carries flow variables between them; a second executor would compete with it.
evidence: The stack's direct-execution check reports no direct-execution finding in any FlowRouterRunner-defining module
The FlowRouterRunner's execute path returns the result of delegating the resolved user/system flow to the FlowRunner's execute entry point (roles.runtime_components#user_system_flow_runner_execute)
verification: Strict disposition, severity 4: a newly introduced direct-execution pattern is not suppressible and fails the check run.

The check flags, in any FlowRouterRunner-defining module: a direct import of a product capability entry module, a call of a direct user/system-flow-execution entry point, and a step-sequence iteration used as an executor loop. How these patterns are recognized concretely is the per-stack detector's concern (profile: layout.locations#capability_entry, roles.runtime_components#direct_user_system_flow_execution, roles.plan_hierarchy#user_system_flow_step_sequence, idiom.source_syntax#step_executor_loop).
The check exempts the production FlowRunner itself: its own step loop is legitimate and not flagged. Which module is the FlowRunner is the per-stack detector's concern.

Scope: every FlowRouterRunner-defining module wherever it lives in the application. Which trees a detector actually scans is the per-stack realization's concern; a narrower scan path (the user/system flows tree in the reference realization) is a detector-scope limitation, not part of the obligation.

fires: Adding or editing any FlowRouterRunner-defining module in the application, wherever it lives
A FlowRouterRunner-defining module gains an import of a product capability entry module, anywhere in the module
Flow router code invokes a direct user/system-flow-execution entry point or iterates a user/system flow's step sequence to run steps
doesNotFire: Editing the production FlowRunner itself, including its own step loop
Changes to product capability modules or other code that never defines a FlowRouterRunner
A tree with no FlowRouterRunner at all (covered by the companion rule that requires one to exist)

neutralityNotes: FlowRouterRunner, FlowRunner, product capability, user/system flow, step sequence and flow variables are the ATDD runtime's own architecture vocabulary (agnostic core spec afokapu/atdd#1251), not stack names, so the core keeps them; it names no stack, runtime, framework, language, package manager, file suffix or path. Everything concrete about recognizing the forbidden patterns is per-stack profile data: the product capability entry module (layout.locations#capability_entry), the direct-execution call (roles.runtime_components#direct_user_system_flow_execution), the user/system flow's step-sequence containment field (roles.plan_hierarchy#user_system_flow_step_sequence) and the executor-loop syntax (idiom.source_syntax#step_executor_loop); the FlowRunner's execution entry point that the positive delegation requires is roles.runtime_components#user_system_flow_runner_execute. How a detector recognizes those constructs in code remains the per-stack realization's concern. The reference detector's src/user-system-flows/** scan scope is narrower than the app-wide obligation; bun.json itself states the path is not a prerequisite, so the core stays app-wide. The language activation fact (typescript/javascript) is stack profile data (tooling.languages) that the realization uses for language gating; 'language' is not a neutral fact kind, so the neutral core does not gate on it. The doesNotFire cross-reference to coder.bun.flow-router-runner-exists was neutralized to 'the companion rule that requires a FlowRouterRunner to exist', since rule ids are realization-scoped.
